newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE to reach for 4,455 after weak start.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE to reach for 4,455 after weak start.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will probably recover to around 4,455 after initial weakness in what may be a slow session on Thursday, the day of the UK election, technical analysts said.
By 0717 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 0.4 at 4,435.6.

On Tuesday, there were about the same number of FTSE stocks going up as those coming down and with the market now so close to its record closing high of 4,444.3, neither the bulls nor the bears seem completely in control, they added.
In normal times, a rise in the Dow would be mimicked by a similar move by the FTSE, but as demonstrated yesterday an initial gain can easily evaporate.

But with today being election day, these aren't normal times and investors sense dangerous times ahead, which has lead to erratic movements by the FTSE and which will continue for some time yet, analysts said.

Over the past two days, the market has edged up on high volume indicating upward pressure but yesterday it looked uncomfortable peering above its previous intra-day high of 4,466.3 -- of March 11 -- and tenaciously held above 4,430.
The market will not necessarily fare much better today but the uptrend since April should should mean it can make a gradual rise.
And with Wall Street finishing higher on Wednesday and many European bourses also in medium-term uptrends, the FTSE should soon shrug off any weakness and venture higher.
On Wednesday, the Dow closed up 46.96 at 7,008.99.
